Details: Communist organizers build pressure across individual states as local cells challenge national control. Controlled areas move from agitation through strongholds to lockdowns, and the crisis can grow into a national revolt. Military action, negotiation, and emergency intervention shape the country's response. The movement remains contained until its final whispers open a path toward world revolution.
Evo I: Gathering Storm: Unstable Revolutionary Activity begins once any state is communist-controlled. Enables rare surprise revolts, including very rare one-state breakaway revolts with rebel armies scaled by state and country strength.
Evo II: Rising Chaos: Dark Worker Rituals begins once a Level 2 stronghold exists. Enables rare worker ritual incidents that disrupt a controlled state, raise intervention risk, improve later conversion chance, and slightly increase communist support.
Evo III: Chaos Tier: Whispers of the World Revolution begins once a Level 3 lockdown exists. Unlocks World Revolution for the major-event pool. Later whisper events add 200 World Revolution weight and mark states as more likely to join uprisings.
World-End Scenario: No terminal world-end. Whispers of the World Revolution hands the communist crisis to the separate World Revolution major event, where controlled states may become revolutionary bases.

Details: A zombie outbreak erupts in a populous state and spreads through crowded, vulnerable regions. Captured land falls under the horde, while each adaptation makes containment harder. Governments balance front-line defense, prevention, cure research, and cooperation with the Anti-Zombie League as secondary outbreaks multiply.
Evo I: Gathering Storm: the first major zombie adaptation makes the horde much harder to starve out and much stronger at night. It is the point where early containment starts slipping, and cure work begins getting harder.
Evo II: Rising Chaos: the horde turns into a faster assault force with better attack pressure and even less reliance on supply. Finding the cure becomes harder again.
Evo III: Chaos Tier: weak fronts can collapse fast, and the cure is at its hardest to finish.
World-End Scenario:
Zombie Apocalypse

The outbreak has outgrown every line built to contain it. The dead move from ruined cities into the last organized refuges, while the living lose the roads, laboratories, and armies needed to answer them.

The Zombie Horde becomes the dominant order of the world. Isolated survivors remain in scattered refuges under a world ordered by the dead.

Details: A Himalayan refuge can become the Holy Realm as its people develop a Bodhisattva-led order, the Arhat Administration, and the Buddha Mandate. Political and spiritual choices shape whether the state follows restraint, peacekeeping, coercive pacification, Divine Sovereignty, or the final doctrine.
Evo I: Mountain Refuge: forms The Holy Realm, initializes Mandala and Buddhahood counters, applies fragile refuge ideas, opens the Mandala GUI/category, loads the focus tree, and starts shelter, road, refugee, early teaching, and defensive play.
Evo II: Bodhisattva Teaching and Meditation: Send Dhamma Envoys, Guard the Pilgrimage Route, Translate the Wheel, teaching-under-fire, and the concentration-vow sequence raise Bodhi, Compassion, Dhyana Depth, and Meditation Charge while tracking clean-route and Defilement risks.
Evo III: Governance, Sanctuary, Guardian, and Sangha Compact routes: Council/Regent/Assembly choices, infrastructure and supply works, Temple Guard and pilgrimage escort systems, compact admission, aid, anti-puppet clauses, and AI weights support defensive humanitarian play against special chaos countries.
Evo IV: The Unshaken Seat and Powers: Buddhahood requires 108 Bodhi, Fourth Dhyana, low Defilements, teaching successes, crisis teaching, and the focus marker. Success changes leader/stage, fires The Awakened One, unlocks the Buddha powers category, and the first anti-chaos power display fires Powers of the Awakened.
Evo V: Final Doctrine and Schism: the hidden False Buddha branch supports debate, exile, suppression, and absorption outcomes. Extinction of Defilements, Witnesses Gather, and the final doctrine balance gate a non-terminal Empty Seat aftermath against a terminal consequence request.

Details: Wars erupt between eligible countries and expand into linked conflict webs as chaos rises. Special countries can join later stages, turning a local declaration into a wider chain of fighting.
Evo I: Gathering Storm: Triangular Incident. Three declarations fire in one linked dispute.
Evo II: Rising Chaos: Four Fronts. Four declarations fire in one conflict web, with a small chance for a compatible special country to appear.
Evo III: Chaos Tier: Contagious Ultimatums. Five declarations fire, major countries and faction members become more likely, and special-country involvement becomes more common.
Evo IV: Totalen Chaos: The War Week. Six declarations fire in a short chain, with a strong chance of one compatible special country participating.
Evo V: World Collapse: Open Season. Seven to eight declarations fire while normal random events still run. Compatible special countries are strongly favored when available.

Details: The Soviet Union loses authority over republics, rail offices, garrisons, and depots. Local ministries and breakaway governments test Moscow with demands for recognition and control. Repression can delay the collapse while deepening famine, fear, and grievance, and the crisis may end in a new settlement or a war over the Union's remains.
Evo I: First Durable Secession: a republic ministry, garrison, or depot network stops obeying Moscow and survives long enough to make its break visible.
Evo II: Regional Cascade: several republics are free, and release pressure spreads through foreign attention, depot weakness, League coordination, and public refusal.
Evo III: Union Unmade: Moscow has lost Union-wide command. Remaining ordinary republics are forced out of the old center, and the former Union enters open war over its borders.
Evo IV: Maximum Rupture: every remaining republic and eligible special splinter can break from the former Union. The crisis becomes a map-wide struggle over who inherits the old state.
Evo V: World Collapse Rupture: the same break reaches its final intensity, forcing the last eligible remnants into the open while the former Union becomes one front among a collapsing world.

Details: Across several regions, provisional states rise together from local claims, prepared institutions, regional identities, and remembered polities. Former hosts retain a remnant while the new governments face unsettled borders, disputed assets, fragile forces, and urgent questions of recognition, government, security, and patronage.
Evo I:
The Manuals Cross the Border

Founding charters, civil-service manuals, recognition protocols, and trusted couriers now pass from one young state to the next. New governments enter the world with stronger institutions, earlier diplomatic contacts, and a network prepared to sponsor their survival.
Evo II:
Old Nations Wake

Dormant national projects and half-remembered unions return to political life. Regional and signature independence movements can surface sooner, while the states already born from the wave gain the confidence and institutions needed to rediscover larger identities.
Evo III:
Flags Rise Behind the Barracks

The next declarations arrive with officers, guarded depots, and plans for immediate defense. Breakaway governments gain stronger military budgets and better prepared forces, but every rifle issued sharpens instability, former-host hostility, and the fear of reconquest.
Evo IV:
The Sovereigns Take Their Seats

The informal network becomes a congress of delegates, observers, and rejected clients. Recognition missions, arbitration, rescue commitments, and a shared reserve draw the independent states toward collective leadership without deciding the charter they must ultimately choose.
Evo V:
No Border Is Final

World collapse strips old borders of their final authority. New sovereignty projects enter the struggle for independence, while existing breakaways gain the freedom and pressure to pursue dangerous routes.

Details: An eligible minor country is swept into Fury and becomes an expansionist war state. Its first conquest opens a wider cycle of reinforcement, rival Fury actors, border pressure, and a possible world-end war.
Evo I: Hardened Fury: unlocks once the first Fury cycle escalates. Future and eligible current Fury actors receive the hardened national spirit, more starting columns, higher momentum, and a stronger sustained reinforcement profile.
Evo II: Second War Table: ensures at least two Fury actors can exist, unlocks cooperation and rivalry content, enables Fury Pact handling, and records the second evolution in the event log.
Evo III: All Borders Burn: ensures up to three Fury actors, strengthens weekly growth, allows all-border declarations, and unlocks the world-end candidate focus path.
World-End Scenario:
The World in Fury

Fury is no longer confined to one rogue state. Armed hosts answer one another across continents, each treating the nearest border as an invitation to attack and every pause as weakness.

A network of Fury states opens a global war and leaves political settlements behind. Rage becomes the world's governing order.

Details: Public accusations, leaked cables, and military bulletins unsettle foreign offices before any government admits that a crisis exists. In calmer periods the alarm chiefly raises international tension. As chaos deepens, repeated incidents poison relations, quicken later crises, push governments toward readiness, and may turn a disputed frontier into a limited clash.
Evo I: Cable Traffic Increase. Cable traffic swells as embassies answer rumours with denials. Relations begin to fray, and each new dispatch makes the next alarm easier to believe.
Evo II: Competing Accusations. Competing accusations spread through more capitals. Delayed reports keep old suspicions alive, while cautious governments quietly raise their readiness.
Evo III: Staff Readiness. General staffs begin treating rumour as warning. Diplomatic shocks linger, frontier incidents become harder to contain, and peaceful governments watch the Thin Wire with growing unease.
Evo IV: Extended Alert. Extended alert becomes the normal condition. Heavier accusations and exhausted border commands make a limited frontier clash more likely as every government insists that peace still holds.

Details: White Peace seeks wars that can end with the same borders and no indemnity or scripted-story damage. Later stages can settle several minor fronts, involve a major country, or quiet a wider diplomatic crisis when the world is overloaded with wars.
Evo I: Repeated Minor Settlements: Repeated Minor Settlements lets one firing quiet several minor fronts when enough safe pairs exist.
Evo II: Major-Country Settlement: Major-Country Settlement allows a rare no-gain exit involving a major country when the wider conflict remains unchanged.
Evo III: Broad Diplomatic Settlement: Broad Diplomatic Settlement lets one armistice circular quiet broader safe war clutter while leaving protected wars untouched.

Details: Death begins as a hidden island crisis and can grow into a global war. It consumes states, empties populations, and leaves wastelands in its wake. The Black Ledger strengthens Death with each loss, while ghost hosts and mainland pressure spread after the first reveal. Living countries answer with investigation, quarantine, recovery, and war as they try to retake every state under Death's control.
Evo I: Second Shore: Death can unlock its first island-spread focus path. Its first spread moves slowly while the mainland route stays closed.
Evo II: Mainland Hunger: Death can press the island pattern faster and unlock the mainland focus path. A valid coastal mainland state can become the public reveal point once enough island pressure exists.
Evo III: First Hosts: Near the 600 chaos mark, Death can gain weak custom ghost divisions with very low organization. They hold borders passively and are much weaker than infantry.
Evo IV: Hollow Hosts: Near the 800 chaos mark, Death can gain more custom ghost divisions with higher organization and strength. They remain weaker than infantry and should still be pushable.
Evo V: World End: Once Death has consumed a full continent and Chaos is above 1000, Death gains many infantry-parity hosts and begins attacking aggressively.
World-End Scenario:
Last Shores

Death has emptied enough land to turn islands, wastelands, and ghost hosts into one design. A consumed continent gives Zol the ground from which to reach every surviving shore.

New footholds open across the living world, and the dead march from the last shores to complete the Black Ledger. No population remains beyond Death's count.

Details: A covert alliance leaves the same traces in distant incidents. Couriers vanish, equipment fails, and quiet methods recur across borders. Following the pattern can expose the network before its next operation.
Evo I:
Repeating Methods

The same routes, tricks, and timings are turning up far beyond the first incidents. Leaks and defections reveal pieces of the connection, even if the full list of partners stays hidden.
Evo II:
Coordinated Interference

The incidents now point to an organized foreign campaign. Covert attacks are growing bolder, and the country must decide whom to suspect, which sources to trust, and how much to prepare.
Evo III:
Approaching Confrontation

Border pressure, military precautions, and nervous public warnings are piling up. The hidden crisis is close to becoming an open confrontation, and the opening moves remain fluid.

Details: An African government begins drawing the continent together through aid, guarantees, liberation agreements, and a common Charter. Other countries can join the project, bargain over its terms, leave it, or build a rival camp. Regional congresses and constitutional settlements decide whether the League becomes roads, armies, laws, and a lasting argument over who carries the cost. The opening also unlocks an armoured war-elephant guard for the preserved host and accepted members, using one shared monumental formation distinct from ordinary elephant regiments. Other strange formations remain separately gated until their own identities are ready. If the Charter host falls, one recorded successor may inherit the ledgers and obligations; otherwise the project remains a visible suspended docket rather than inventing a new government. The Scramble opens six distinct external-continent packages: Middle East, Europe, Asia, North America, South America, and Oceania. Each package has a dedicated constitutional route, decisions, AI behaviour, an emblem, fictional male steward portraits, localisation, and installers for existing governments. W5's all-six certification is source-wired behind frozen roster proof. Actions 85-92 remain gated by the political state rather than missing assets. The World has its own terminal emblem and final super-event, achievement, flag, and audio contract; unique models are outside this pass.
Evo I:
Regional Consolidation

The Charter League has kept its first promise and can finally look beyond one corridor. Regional congresses, negotiated settlements, restoration claims, and rival blocs will decide whether its protection grows into lasting cooperation.
Evo II:
Continental Machinery

The League is settling into daily life. Shared railways, emergency forces, membership law, and resource bargains tie distant courts together, and every new connection brings another bill or obligation.
Evo III:
Africa as a World Pole

Africa's settlement has become a question every great power must answer. Foreign bases, sanctions, continent-wide mobilization, strange new actors, and rival projects are now part of the same struggle.
World-End Scenario:
The World Is One

The final settlement closes the last continental rivalries. The host reaches The World through a recorded unanimous union, last-standing settlement, or continental campaign. The terminal super-event ONE WORLD REMAINS, achievement, flag, audio, and distinct emblem identify the final order. W5's all-six package certification is source-wired and awaits frozen-roster political proof. Actions 85-92 remain gated by the required political state rather than missing assets. Unique models are intentionally outside this pass.

Details: Rivers burst their banks, faults split open, storms tear through rail lines, ash buries farms, and wildfires outrun the roads. Each disaster leaves a local fight to rescue survivors, steady the region, and rebuild before the next emergency arrives.
Evo I:
Wider Disaster Seasons

Bad seasons bring several disasters close together. Rescue crews, supplies, and safe roads become harder to share when every region seems to need them at once.
Evo II:
Regional Cascades

The damage spills across state lines. Broken transport, hunger, disease, refugees, and exhausted reconstruction crews turn one ruined region into a problem for all its neighbors.
Evo III:
Abnormal Paths

The disasters begin moving in impossible ways. Ruptures, meteors, ash clouds, storms, tornadoes, and tsunamis travel across whole regions, giving countries only a rough idea of where the next blow will land.

Details: Burial parties vanish from an army at war. Ration books are quietly changed, bodies are cut apart, and frightened soldiers suspect that officers protect the killers. The front must keep its units fed while witnesses disappear and organized predators recruit inside the ranks.
Evo I:
Ritualized Ranks

Scattered predators now share oaths, marks, ranks, and protection. The cells recognize one another, and their headquarters remains unknown.
Evo II:
The Organized Network

Cells in different countries use the same ledgers, courier routes, prisoner rules, and attack schedules. The network is clearly organized around a hidden center.
Evo III:
Hannibal Lecter Commands

Hannibal Lecter steps into public view and begins drawing the mature network into one command.
World-End Scenario:
The World Is the Larder

Lecter's host has pulled the feeding territories and armed kitchens into one command. Roads, farms, prisons, and conquered cities are all treated as parts of the same larder. Surviving countries are reduced to prey, raiders, or small resistance enclaves.

The network has no reason to hide anymore. Every government still standing faces an expanding host that intends to feed on the whole world.

No Thaw Will Come

Lecter's winter host has given itself to the Wendigo hunger. Feeding grounds spread with the cold, and conquered communities are dragged into a world where thaw, harvest, and mercy are treated as weaknesses.

Winter advances with the host. Every surviving country is hunted until human rule is consumed or driven into a handful of frozen refuges.

Details: A translated manifesto slips out of reading rooms and into the government of a small country. It promises that common stores, useful work, and public need can build a fairer society. Its readers divide over who decides what people need and how much freedom the plan can afford. Shortages, public works, local charters, and deals with neighbors put every promise to the test.
Evo I:
Glosses in the Margin

Everyone has started writing in the manifesto's margins. Workers, parishes, councils, families, and exiles bring their own copies and their own answers. The movement's future may belong to whoever keeps the right to edit the book.
Evo II:
Necessary Shores

Migration, blockades, crowded homes, and thin supplies push the common store to its limits. Surveyors search for harbors, corridors, settlements, and leases that can meet real needs while preserving the commonwealth's neighbors.
Evo III:
Cities of One Measure

The plan has escaped the capital. Towns and rebuilt districts are opening gardens, clinics, workshops, stores, and transport links of their own. Local votes and local shortages shape each version, and arguments over work reveal who really gets to change the plan.
Evo IV:
Nowhere Made Law

The manifesto now has a place in regional politics. Governments quote it when they ask for aid, defend local charters, refuse threats, or seek association. Small states must decide whether the commonwealth looks like a refuge, a useful partner, or an ambitious neighbor.
Evo V:
The Perfect Island

The world around the commonwealth is coming apart. Reserve trains, guarded harbors, refugee districts, fortifications, and member councils all compete for the same supplies. One path closes the gates and demands service from everyone inside. The other shares refuge among willing towns and spreads the burden across the league.

Details:
Doctor Warren Kruger arrives with working results in fields that rarely fit inside one career, much less one mind. A government can hire him openly, hide him inside a Directorate, or point his talents somewhere else. Wherever he settles, universities, factories, armies, and foreign spies gather around the same guarded rooms.

Kruger's laboratory soon becomes an institution with secrets and ambitions of its own. Everyone accepts that he is brilliant. The government must still prove it can command what his brilliance creates.
Evo I:
National Scientific Ascendancy

Kruger's laboratory has become part of national life. His methods are spreading through universities, factories, hospitals, and military planning.
Evo II:
The International Scientific Contest

Foreign governments are courting Kruger, copying his work, and sending people to steal it. The scientific race is becoming a struggle between states.
Evo III:
Forbidden and Autonomous Science

The Directorate is repeating experiments that ordinary ministries can barely understand, much less supervise. Every dangerous success draws more people and facilities into Kruger's private network.
Evo IV:
Sovereign Science

Kruger has stopped asking permission. He arrives with a demand for political authority and the backing of laboratories, staff, and machines that answer to him.
World-End Scenario:
Laboratory World

Kruger's Directorate has swallowed the governments that once tried to supervise it. Countries, populations, and whole landscapes survive as controlled samples inside a planetary laboratory.

The world has become one experiment, and Kruger alone decides what happens to the control group.

The Strategic Singularity

The Directorate's final device tears through armies, cities, and the air itself. The blast leaves mass death, poisoned ground, and governments too broken to hold the old world together.

The Singularity ends Kruger's experiment and leaves the surviving governments unable to preserve the old order.

Details: A small neutral country is running out of room to stand alone. The great blocs offer protection, weapons, and a seat at their table, sending their envoys toward the next exposed border. Neutrality becomes a political and military struggle fought through councils, troops, and public resolve.
Evo I:
Regional Bloc Race

One accession starts a regional scramble. Border guards dig in, observers arrive, neutrality councils meet, and faction officers make themselves comfortable in nearby capitals.
Evo II:
Pressured Neutrality

War makes neutrality harder to sell. Countries beside active fronts receive sharper demands, louder promises, and less time to answer.
Evo III:
Collapse of Neutrality

Several small states can be pulled toward rival blocs in quick succession. The last neutral capitals answer with hurried councils, guarded borders, and expensive promises to stand alone.

Details: Surveyors have struck a major deposit in one of the country's states. The first find promises jobs, trade, and new industry. Repeated discoveries can turn the same field into a boomtown, a diplomatic prize, or something much harder to control.
Evo I: One field keeps giving. New deposits appear beneath old workings, and foreign buyers, rival claimants, and would-be peacekeepers all want a share of the wealth.
Evo II: Miners fall sick, metal corrodes overnight, people vanish, and something attacks in the lower workings. The country must investigate, contain the danger, or close the field before the boomtown becomes a grave.
Evo III: A huge mixed deposit pulls the workings far below safe ground. Attacks reach the surface, and the country must hunt what escaped, evacuate the field, or seal away every valuable shaft before the breach fully opens.
Evo IV: The field opens into an Oth-Kesh origin chamber. Armored broods pour through the workings, feed on rich deposits, and attack every country they can reach as they search for roads beneath the next continent.
World-End Scenario: The World Opens Below: The first continent is no longer a contained theater. Stronger formations will emerge through resource-weighted footholds on distant continents at once.

Details: Fully formed military units appear across the world with no recruitment orders, training records, or known home. Governments suddenly have to feed, equip, command, and watch soldiers who arrived ready to march. Strange weapons, ambitious commanders, and nonhuman troops can turn a windfall into a rival army.
Evo I:
Organized Muster

The soldiers from nowhere now have district staffs, proper rolls, and officers the government can actually hold responsible.
Evo II:
Arsenal Lottery

New formations arrive carrying baffling mixes of weapons and gear. Each one needs its own training, spare parts, and supply plan.
Evo III:
Command Fracture

Some new commanders inspire more loyalty than the government that received them. Their private authority can split an army or put a claimant in the capital.
Evo IV:
Anomalous Muster

Some arriving hosts are nonhuman. Governments weigh quartering, bargaining, or turning them away before an armed camp becomes a country of its own.

Details:
A black-marked fever has broken out on the mainland. It moves through roads, ports, hungry cities, and rat-filled ruins, leaving governments to choose which places to isolate and which people they can still save.

If the plague is allowed to settle in, the rats may become something more dangerous than carriers. Whole warrens can learn to fight, govern, and follow a king of their own.
Evo I:
The Strain Grows Stronger

The plague has learned to thrive in crowded and poorly protected places. Deaths rise faster, and every untreated corridor helps the next wave spread.
Evo II:
The Plague Crosses the Sea

Ports and long-distance transport carry the plague beyond its mainland cradle. Docks, troop convoys, refugees, and wartime shipping can open a second front across the sea.
Evo III:
The Warrens Raise Flags

Collapsed plague basins have joined one Rat Nation. Its broods seize infected ground and build armies without human soldiers or ordinary equipment.
Evo IV:
The Rat King Wakes

A royal basin has learned to obey one sentient ruler. The Rat King gathers memory, hunger, and authority as the surviving broods decide whether to kneel.
Evo V:
The Kingdom of Teeth

The Rat King's dominion has grown beyond the warrens. Capitals fall silent, refuges are overrun, and the last continental cordons begin to break.
World-End Scenario:
The Kingdom of Teeth

The Black Plague has crossed the final threshold. The sentient Rat King has completed its royal route, seized the required capitals and refuge nodes, and brought an eligible continent under one crown. The final order carries human administrations, surviving infrastructure, and the world itself into a new order ruled from the Royal Basin.

Details: A random country fractures into rival governments and armed camps.
A violent antisemitic faction emerges during the Spanish Civil War, seeks an alliance with Nazi Germany, and threatens Jewish communities across Europe.
Soviet scientists secretly develop nuclear weapons before the wider world expects them.
A Swedish war game movement grants its divisions new tactical training and battlefield advantages.
A race for alien technology in Antarctica can unlock advanced jet research for the country that secures the site.
A government considers moving industry into the desert to preserve living space on the mainland.
A major country gains a complete military doctrine after a sudden research breakthrough.

Scientists track a large asteroid and race to predict its impact. A correct prediction brings a research windfall, while an unexpected strike destroys industry and kills people in the affected states.
A chance discovery brings a country a large political windfall and turns one state into a source of continuing income.

A time traveler known as “Time Traveler” advises a country and warns certain governments against wars that history says they will lose. A later route can bring Napoleon back, followed by a robot invasion from the future.
Evo I: Time Traveler: a historical warning system guides governments away from wars that history says they will lose.
Evo IV: Napoleon returns (Pretzel Logic), World End scenario: army of robots from the future invade, basically like in the movie Terminator.

Details: Violence erupts in a random country, damaging buildings and killing civilians.
Missile technology spreads across the world.
Acid rain crosses continents, reducing populations and damaging affected states.
A random major country enters an industrial boom and doubles its production efficiency.
A major country is hit by a deep economic downturn.
A country recovers an alien spacecraft and receives a fleet of jet fighters plus the means to produce more.
A major country receives millions of unexplained new recruits.
Malta becomes independent, raises knightly armies, claims Mediterranean territory, and wages a new crusade. Later stages can place the Pope in Rome at the head of a Kingdom of God.
Evo IV: A dedicated crusader route opens. Failure leads to an eleventh crusade, while success expands the conquests, adopts The Holy See identity, installs the Pope as leader, and makes Rome the holy capital of a Kingdom of God.

Details: A random country's leader is murdered, leaving the government to face a succession crisis.
A random Arabian country falls under British control through a Lawrence of Arabia intervention.
A mysterious shipment falls from the sky, changing a country's military prospects.
A country receives a sudden shipment of military equipment.
A massive flood devastates every coastal state it reaches.
The major powers enter a race to reach space.
The Balkan states plunge into a third regional war.
No active earthquake scenario is available for this event.
A mysterious explosion destroys a random province and may resemble a nuclear strike.
Bulgaria revives claims over its historic lands.
A mad scientist's warning spreads mass panic through the country.
A major country is cut off by a global embargo.
A heat wave sweeps across the world as a separate crisis.
A major country's intelligence becomes exposed to every government.
A sudden scientific breakthrough spreads across the world.
A country enters a sudden infrastructure boom.
A naval renaissance gives every country a functioning fleet.
Radar coverage expands across the world.
Industry expands in every country as factories spread with the territory under control.
Every country expands its civilian industry in proportion to the territory it controls.
Every country adopts a more aggressive strategic posture.
A research setback leaves a nation with only two research slots. A Kruger Directorate can preserve its current capacity at a concrete political and institutional cost.
Half of each country's military factories become civilian factories.
A faction expels a random member and declares war on it.
A random puppet breaks free and becomes independent.
Country leaders develop unexpected talents.
Every country leader receives a random trait.
International market funding expands for a random major country.
A random country elevates one general to the rank of Generalissimo and gives him exceptional ability.
People from another universe called ZIN settle in a state and its neighbors. They claim neutrality, yet a war against them unleashes a supernatural reprisal.
Evo IV: Later waves bring several alien invasions, each with a distinct weakness.

Details: A Boxer Rebellion erupts in China.
African gods predict a world consumed by chaos. Prayer can delay disasters, while neglect makes each wave faster and more destructive until the campaign faces ruin.
Iran restores the Persian Empire and attacks every country holding Persian cores.
Ireland attacks the holder of Northern Ireland. The conflict can end when Ireland secures the region.
Mongolia revives a steppe empire, gains claims on its neighbors, and raises large cavalry forces.
Japan seizes California during its war with the United States.
Tannu Tuva joins the Allies or God's Plan when that faction exists.
The United States tests new weapons in another country's territory.
A major country or the player sends stored equipment to a random minor ally.
A border conflict erupts between the player and a random neighbor.
A hidden master pressures a random minor country to follow a rival or opposing ideology.
A giant tourist airship leaves the United States on a round-the-world voyage. If it crashes, the United States gains a war goal and the impact can damage the state or start a wildfire.
Britain imposes taxes on every country.
Every country moves one step toward total mobilization.
A sudden windfall places political power in every government.
A surge of military experience raises every country's commanders.
Every country receives 100 army, navy, or air experience of its chosen type.
Germany or the Soviet Union proclaims a claim to the world.
A temporary military emergency boosts entrenchment across the world.
Governments form technology-sharing networks.
Kamikaze doctrine spreads to every country.
Every country gains access to kamikaze strikes.

Lenin returns with a third eye and an army of humanoid workers. The revolution spreads through states in proportion to communist support, while defecting communists gain power and slowly become part of the monster host. Stalin and Trotsky fight Lenin as the movement grows.
Evo IV: Strange worker strikes foreshadow Lenin's return. Later stages expose the anomalous forces, strengthen Lenin's powers, and draw communist leaders into the transformation.

Details: Countries compete to buy Greenland.
Portugal demands Galicia from Spain.
A random major country or the player loses half of its equipment stockpiles.
An exiled country launches a revolt from occupied territory. When no occupation exists, a dormant claimant can appear before any war begins.
Division templates become temporarily unavailable to every country.
Countries establish collaboration networks against one another.
A country discovers a new metal that improves armor production in the state it controls. Other governments can seek access to the resource through agreements.
A Dust and Sandstorm crisis reaches the selected country once Wider Disaster Seasons is available. This entry uses the Natural Disasters event family.
Inflation grips major countries and the player. Stability rises or falls with the crisis, and a prolonged failure can bring political upheaval or civil war.
Countries face timed tasks whose failure brings harmful consequences.
A serial killer terrorizes a country through a chain of murders. The investigation follows a chain of choices, and a mistake sends it back to the beginning.
Low war support pushes conscription downward, while strong war support enables higher conscription.
Each country weighs stability against war support, gaining one while sacrificing the other.
A player's ideology faces temporary decline and public discontent. Protest movements are weaker when support is high, while a collapse below one percent can trigger regime change or civil war.
A paranoia crisis spreads through a country in a manner similar to the Soviet Union crisis.
A random rule becomes active and changes the campaign.
A small non-island country launches an expansionist campaign.
A new national spirit appears in every country.
Occupied states erupt in resistance across major countries and the player.
A chest market introduces common, rare, and epic prizes to a country's political life.
A national wrestling tournament turns one contender into a public hero.
A wrestling tournament rewards the champion after countries train their chosen contender.
A worldwide fuel crisis leaves every country with no stored fuel.
A Macedonian uprising turns the slogan Freedom or Death into a national crisis.
Spartan warriors rise in Greece.
A major country or the player faces five rival camps in a civil war. Stability and ideology support shape the opening balance, while alliances can postpone the final duel.
A plague of locusts travels across the world and brings famine to affected regions.
A new regional alliance forms in a random part of the world.
A massive volcanic eruption turns the states around a random volcanic region into wasteland.
The strongest country in a random ideology proposes a pact in which every member guarantees the others.
Cossacks rise from a random East Slavic state and expand across East Slavia.
Several neighbors claim a random country and divide its territory or fight for it.
Countries at peace demilitarize every state except their capital until war allows remilitarization.
Two random countries sign a non-aggression pact.
A religious faction forms with the goal of destroying rival religions.
Subject governments demand greater autonomy.
Every subject receives autonomy points.
A regional shaman offers aid to the major country that controls the surrounding area.
Tomorrow's Girls brings alien companions into national politics, and a leader can gain manpower through their influence.
Countries with low war support face army mutinies as units turn against their commands.
A government invests in military, civilian, naval, or special industry.

Countries holding non-core states face independence movements shaped by Gandhi's principles of nonviolence, noncooperation, truth, and honesty. Denial removes the value of occupation while unrest spreads, with fascist governments affected differently.
Countries face a sudden surplus of military equipment.
Every country receives a choice of large equipment grants.
A research surge focuses each country on one field.
Every country receives a choice of research investment in one category.
A mountain and hill country forms the Mountain Republic and claims every matching state.
A creature feeds on crops and people in a random major country or the player, spreading fear until it is hunted.

Dracula terrorizes Transylvania and can found the Vampire Kingdom, which attacks its former controller and England before threatening the world. The one-battalion “Count Dracula” unit decides the kingdom's fate, and neighbors receive the “Fear of Dracula” national spirit until they confront it.
Whispers drive mass suicides in a random major country or the player. As deaths spread, generals and leaders can disappear until the country itself collapses.
A major country or player with strong ideological support faces partisan divisions, some of them armored, in proportion to its support.
A rock-paper-scissors contest decides a territorial dispute. Victory transfers the state, while defeat costs part of the player's industry.
Subjects across the world declare independence and form the National Liberation Front. Their former masters can accept the separation or fight the simultaneous wars.
Intelligence agencies expand their clandestine networks.
Counterintelligence improves across the world.
Every country gains one point of counterintelligence.
Pacifism rises again as a political force.
A migration crisis drains people from a random major country or the player toward neighboring states. Stability and living conditions shape the severity of the loss.

A shadowy society known as “Secret Society Influence” affects a government's ministers and generals, causing confusion and distrust. The national spirit reduces stability and political power while increasing consumer goods demand.
A teleportation experiment makes one division vanish. A later breakthrough can move several divisions and shorten the cooldown.
Evo IV: A teleportation breakthrough moves multiple divisions and shortens the cooldown.

Details: A conspiracy-theorist movement forms.
A random major country guarantees a random minor.
New Zealand begins questioning its own existence.
A prophet travels the world preaching peace, leaving sayings in every country he visits.
A travelling man reaches the United States and leaves behind a series of disruptive events.
Every country moves its capital to a random state.
An alien invasion begins through the mysterious song "Tomorrow's Girls" by Donald Fagen. A social game asks whether each girl is human or alien.
A vision of a unified world of salads and sun spreads across the campaign.
Shark-infested waters increase casualties whenever ships sink.
The Devil offers power in exchange for escalating bargains. Accepting more deals deepens the demonic influence, while refusal can bring new offers and harsher consequences before the pact is broken.
Evo IV: The demonic influence reaches a second visual stage, with the leader's eyes changing.

Details: Alien fears lead the United States to form an anti-alien coalition, with its leader adopting a tinfoil hat.
A mysterious doctor appears with a cure for every disease.
Mr. LaPage is a dangerous kidnapper inspired by the song Everyone's Gone to the Movies.
A futuristic car travels the world.
The campaign can end in the Custerdome when chaos stays low through 1944, opening a rare place of wealth and peace.
A strange shuffle swaps national values, turning one measure into another.
Good King Richard and Good King John are crowned, blending Richard the Lionheart, King John, Richard Nixon, and John Kennedy in a double royal succession inspired by the song "Kings".
Special technologies, such as nuclear submarines, appear for a random major country.
A shortage of a random resource spreads through the world.
Drug use spreads through society, forcing governments to confront addiction.
A government pursues a super-soldier serum through a biowarfare special project. Testing on apes can lead to an uprising.
Evo IV: Animal testing can trigger an ape uprising.

Details: When pretenders and crises multiply, Jesus appears to guide a lost world, inspired by the song Jesus Came Down by Lake.
A card system starts with three common cards and expands to six slots as the collection reaches milestones. Chests and completed challenges add more cards.
A hidden bomb threat grows through a chain of choices inspired by Lake's song Time Bomb.
The Crazy Scientist concept is absorbed into Brilliant Scientist and its Kruger Directorate.
A dangerous disease opens a race to master biological weapons and the power of death.
A random country receives new strategic facilities.
Governments announce a wave of completed special projects.
A chain of unsettling incidents leads a country toward the mystery of The White Ribbon.
A casino crisis turns stability, war support, political power, and experience into wagers inspired by Hearts of Gamble.
A rare Friday event makes everything heavily discounted for one day.
